extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent practitioners (USPTO prosecution audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive criteria governing entry, non-entry, expedited processing, and handling of amendments and replies after final action, after allowance, and related USPTO practice (MPEP guidance). Directed at examiners and applicants for correct prosecution handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely mailing to avoid abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Every effort should be made to mail the letter before the period for reply expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no appeal has been filed within the period for reply and no amendment has been submitted to make the application allowable or which can be entered in part (see MPEP § 714.20), the application stands abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.181 petitions do not stay reply periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.181(f), the filing of a 37 CFR 1.181 petition will not stay the period for reply to an examiner’s action which may be running against an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1206 for appeal and post-appeal procedure. For after-final practice relative to affidavits or declarations filed under 37 CFR 1.131 and 1.132, see MPEP § 715.09 and § 716.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Advisory Action form paragraph 7.169
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.169 may be used to notify applicant in the Advisory Action that the proposed amendment(s) will be entered upon appeal and how the new or amended claim(s) would be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When used: specify claim(s) that would be rejected and identify the rejection by reference to the final Office action; repeat paragraph for each group of claims; use when PTOL-303 item 7 checked indicating entry upon appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand delivery location and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Hand carried papers for the Technology Centers (TCs) may only be delivered to the Customer Window at the Randolph Building (Customer Service Window, 401 Dulany Street, Alexandria, VA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective Dec. 1, 2003, all official patent application related correspondence that is hand-carried must be delivered to the Customer Window, with limited exceptions. Hand-carried amendments and other replies after final rejection (37 CFR 1.116) will no longer be accepted in the TCs. Patent application related CDs and other non-paper submissions that are hand-carried must be delivered to the Customer Window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited procedure for processing replies after final rejection (37 CFR 1.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: To use expedited processing, the amendment/reply under 37 CFR 1.116 must be marked 'Reply under 37 CFR 1.116 — Expedited Procedure - Technology Center (Insert Technology Center Number)' on the upper right of the paper, and the envelope must be marked 'Mail Stop AF' in the lower left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markings should preferably be in a bright color. Envelope should contain only replies under 37 CFR 1.116. Mail to 'Mail Stop AF, Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia, 22313-1450' or hand-carry to Customer Window. Upon receipt envelope is specially processed, forwarded to TC; SPE ensures prompt action; USPTO goal: mail examiner's action within 1 month of receipt. Benefits require proper markings; procedure cannot overcome applicant-caused delays (e.g., delayed interviews, further replies, petitions). If delay beyond target plus normal mailing time, contact SPE or TC Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quayle action (Ex parte Quayle) and shortened reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: When application is in condition for allowance except for formal matters, prosecution on the merits is closed under Ex parte Quayle and a shortened statutory period for reply (TWO MONTHS) is set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.51 to issue an Ex parte Quayle action. Explain the formal matters which must be corrected in the form paragraph bracket.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendment as of right after Notice of Allowance (37 CFR 1.312 general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may be made as a matter of right in an application after the mailing of the notice of allowance; any amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 must be filed before or with payment of the issue fee and may be entered on recommendation of the primary examiner approved by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after allowance broadly include changes to spec, drawings, claims, inventorship, submission of prior art, petitions to correct spelling/order of inventors, etc. An amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 must be filed on or before date the issue fee is paid, except as required by Office of Patent Publication (PUBS).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.312 compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 and approval authority
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 must comply with the provisions of 37 CFR 1.121; Director has delegated approval of recommendations under 37 CFR 1.312 to supervisory patent examiners (SPEs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiner may make examiner's amendments and enter corrections of formal matters, claim cancellations, or formal claim changes without forwarding to SPE; other amendments that change scope require SPE approval. Supplemental reissue oath/declaration is treated as an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 for reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required remarks accompanying amendments affecting disclosure/scope/claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For amendments affecting the disclosure, scope of any claim, or adding a claim, the remarks must fully and clearly state: (A) why the amendment is needed; (B) why the proposed amended or new claims require no additional search or examination; (C) why the claims are patentable; and (D) why they were not presented earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirements of 37 CFR 1.111(c) with respect to pointing out the patentable novelty of any claim sought to be added or amended apply to amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 as in ordinary amendments. See MPEP §§ 713.04 and 713.10 regarding interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.312 not for continued prosecution; adequate reasons for non-entry
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.312 was never intended to provide a way for continued prosecution after an application has been passed for issue; when recommendation is against entry a detailed statement is not necessary — a simple statement that the proposed claim is not obviously allowable and briefly why is usually adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient reasons include: (A) an additional search is required; (B) more than a cursory review of the record is necessary; or (C) the amendment would involve materially added work on the part of the Office (e.g., checking excessive editorial changes). Dependent-claim-only additions are less likely to be refused, but new matter, sufficiency of disclosure, or undue multiplicity could arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed after payment of issue fee not permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendments should be filed after the date the issue fee has been paid; 37 CFR 1.312 no longer permits filing an amendment after the issue fee is paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 13.10 to notify applicant that an amendment filed after payment of the issue fee will not be entered. See MPEP § 607 for related fee issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and handling of amendments under 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 that affect disclosure, add claims, or change claim scope are sent by OIPE to Publishing Division which forwards to the Technology Center; IFW applications use OIPE Central Scanning and IFW procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receipt TC promptly processes and a designated technical support staff forwards to the examiner via SPE. Examiner indicates 'Enter — 312', 'Do Not Enter' or 'Enter In Part' in red ink on amendment. If favorably considered, it's entered and PTO-271 (Response to Rule 312 Communication) is prepared and signed by primary examiner (or SPE if required). If adverse, reasons for nonentry are typed on PTO-271. The file, drawing, and unmailed notices are forwarded to SPE for consideration, approval and mailing. IFW-specific scanning and document coding procedures apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments embodying only formal corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments that embody merely the correction of formal matters in the specification, formal changes in a claim without changing scope, or cancellation of claims may be entered without SPE prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner indicates approval of such amendments by writing 'Enter Formal Matters Only' thereon. Such amendments do not require submission to the SPE prior to entry. If disapproved in whole or part they require SPE signature. IFW processing guidance: print first page, write 'Enter' and scan with appropriate code.

rubrics_metrics.name: PUBS-required amendments after issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office of Patent Publication (PUBS) discovers an error in preparation for issuance (missing text, drawing inconsistency, etc.), PUBS may require an amendment even after payment of issue fee and has delegated authority to waive 37 CFR 1.312 to accept such amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PUBS may accept and process these amendments without withdrawing the application from issue. These PUBS-required amendments may be hand delivered to PUBS (South Tower Building, 2900 Crystal Drive, Room 8A24, Arlington, VA) or faxed to the provided number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry-in-part of 37 CFR 1.312 amendments (when appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: General rule: an amendment should not be entered in part; however, when strict observance would cause harm, acceptable portions should be entered and unacceptable portions denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) substitute specification unacceptable but other amendments acceptable — enter the rest and deny substitute spec; (B) 1.312 amendments partially approved are entered only as to approved part; (C) after Ex Parte Quayle, amendments curing only formal defect may be entered but new claims are not a right; (D) amendments accompanying a motion granted in part are entered to the extent motion granted. Examiner writes 'Enter' in red ink and initials opposite enterable portions. Applicant should be advised which changes were entered. Entry-in-part not recommended unless full additional fee (if any) accompanies the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed after the period for reply has expired
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is filed after the period set for reply without a petition for extension and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a), such amendment shall be placed in the file but not formally entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff shall immediately notify applicant by telephone and letter that the amendment was not timely and cannot be entered and that the application is abandoned unless a petition for extension of time and the appropriate fee are timely filed. See MPEP § 711.02 and § 710.02(e) for 37 CFR 1.136(a) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date stamping and priority of amendments (Technology Center vs Office Date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in paper files are stamped with the date of receipt in the Technology Center (Technology Center Date) and with the Office Date (date of receipt by the Office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Office Date in writing to the applicant regarding the amendment. Mail deliveries should be screened to remove amendments replying to a final action where a time period is running against applicant — these should be processed within the next 24 hours. After entry the application is forwarded to the examiner who inspects the amendment per MPEP § 714.05. Evaluation of compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 should be left to the examiner; if non-compliant, attach a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment to the advisory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendment types ordinarily denied entry
rubrics_metrics.description: The following types of amendments are ordinarily denied entry: (A) presenting an unpatentable claim or a claim requiring a new search or raising a new issue in an application whose prosecution before the primary examiner has been closed; (B) substitute specification that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.125; (C) a patent claim suggested by the examiner and not presented within the time limit unless Director authorizes; (D) copied patent claims may be refused entry under certain conditions; (E) unsigned or improperly signed amendments or signed by suspended/excluded attorney/agent; (F) amendments filed after expiration of statutory period or set time period for reply; (G) amendments so worded they cannot be entered with certain accuracy; (H) amendment canceling all claims and presenting no substitute claims; (I) amendments in an application no longer within examiner’s jurisdiction except on Director approval; (J) drawings held by examiner to contain new matter not entered until question settled; (K) amendatory paper containing objectionable remarks under 37 CFR 1.3; (L) amendments not in permanent ink or on easily erasable paper; (M) amendments presenting more claims than paid for without fees; (N) amendment canceling all claims drawn to elected invention and presenting only nonelected invention claims (nonresponsive); (O) amendments not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121; (P) preliminary amendments that unduly interfere with preparation of first Office action (37 CFR 1.115(b)); (Q) supplemental replies not filed during suspension period under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While amendments within these categories should not be entered at filing, a subsequent showing by applicant may lead to entry. See referenced MPEP sections for details and exceptions (e.g., copied patent claims, IFW, reissue oaths).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry mechanics: numbering, file placement, IFW handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When several amendments are made on same day, treat as composite single paper where possible. The amendment/letter is placed in the file, given its paper number, and its character endorsed on the file wrapper in red ink; for IFW amendments are entered as papers into the IFW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After entry the application is 'up for action' and forwarded to the examiner who is responsible for proper disposal; examiner should immediately inspect the amendment per MPEP § 714.05. If no immediate or special action required, application awaits examination in regular order. Technical support staff handle initial processing but should not evaluate 37 CFR 1.121 compliance before forwarding to examiner.
